title: Membrane Filtration for SARS-CoV-2 Viral Capture
author: Caleb Centrell
materials: Eppendorf Research Plus Single Channel Pipette

Prepare and collect all supplies necessary for the number of samples that will be concentrated using membrane filtration. All glassware, membrane filtration cups, and centrifuge bottles should be autoclaved with aluminum foil covering any opening Place all autoclaved and sterilized materials underneath the sterilized biological hood Place a biohazard benchtop waste bag into the biological hood on a stand for easy disposal of any contaminated material used during the procedure

Using an Eppendorf Research Plus Single Channel Pipette, place 400 µL of Buffer RLT Qiagen Catalog #79216 from the Qiagen RNeasy Mini Kit (Cat. No. 74106) into the labeled sample DNA LoBind tube that contains the first sample membrane filter paper. The total volume of Buffer RLT will be 800 µL. However, the tube will overflow if it is all added at once. Therefore, only 400 µL is aliquoted to submerge the first filter paper (to prevent it from drying out) while the second paper filters the remaining sample volume in the membrane filtration cup. After the second filter is added to the tube, aliquot the remaining 400 µL of Buffer RLT.

Using an Eppendorf Research Plus Single Channel Pipette, place 800 µL of Buffer RLT Qiagen Catalog #79216 from the Qiagen RNeasy Mini Kit (Cat. No. 74106) into the labeled sample DNA LoBind tube that contains the membrane filter paper.
Place all benchtop paper and all disposable materials into the benchtop biohazard bag.
Aliquot 700 µL of Buffer RW1 Qiagen Catalog #1053394 to the RNeasy spin column. Centrifuge for 00:00:30 at full speed. Discard filtrate.
Aliquot 500 µL of Buffer RPE Qiagen Catalog #1018013 to the RNeasy spin column. Centrifuge for 00:00:30 at full speed. Discard filtrate.
Aliquot 500 µL of Buffer RPE Qiagen Catalog #1018013 to the RNeasy spin column. Centrifuge for 00:02:00 at full speed. Discard filtrate.
Carefully light a alcohol lamp burner.

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Prepare the grab sample for centrifugation under a sterilized biological hood.

substeps.instruction: Remove grab sample from 4°C refrigerator and place under the sterilized biological hood.
Aseptically pour 300 mL of the grab sample into a labeled, autoclaved 500 mL beaker.
Aseptically transfer the 300 mL sample into a labeled, autoclaved centrifuge bottle, ensuring the O-ring is securely inside the lid.
Secure the lid by turning it a quarter turn past tight.
Balance the centrifuge bottle using a benchtop scale (sterilized with 10% bleach then 70% ethanol) located inside the hood; adjust weight with DI water to within 0.5 g of other bottles.
Centrifuge the sample at 5000 rpm for 5 minutes using a Sorvall™ RC 6 Plus centrifuge.
Carefully remove the sample from the centrifuge and return it to the biological hood without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Sample Chemical Treatment and pH Adjustment
steps.instruction: Treat the centrifuged sample with BRSV and MgCl2, and adjust the pH.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL of BRSV aliquot to the sample using an Eppendorf Research Plus Single Channel Pipette, expelling the full volume to the second stop; use a new tip for each sample.
Measure 0.71 g (+/- 0.02 g) of MgCl2 using a benchtop scale and autoclaved chemical spatula.
Place the MgCl2 into the 500 mL beaker used previously, add a magnetic stir bar, and stir for 15 minutes.
Aseptically pour the centrifuged sample (excluding any pellet or solids) into the beaker containing MgCl2 to achieve a final concentration of 25 mM.
Sterilize a calibrated pH probe (excluding the glass measurement part) and the workspace with 10% bleach followed by 70% ethanol.
Adjust the pH to 3.5 +/- 0.1 using 5% HCl and 5% NaOH solutions, using separate pipette droppers for each.
Cover the beaker opening with aluminum foil, securing it with wrapping or autoclave tape.
Gently swirl the sample to ensure homogeneous mixing of BRSV.
Store the sample beaker in a 4°C refrigerator for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Vacuum Manifold Setup
steps.instruction: Prepare the membrane filtration apparatus while the sample is refrigerating.

substeps.instruction: Place an autoclaved membrane filtration cup into each vacuum manifold opening and secure with a quarter turn.
Remove the top cup portion and place it topside down on benchtop paper.
Using sterilized forceps, aseptically place a 0.45 µM membrane filter paper onto the cup opening.
Reattach the top of the membrane filtration cup to the base.
Re-sterilize the forceps and place them in an aseptic position.

steps.title: Primary Membrane Filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the sample through the membrane and collect the filter.

substeps.instruction: Pour 150 mL of the refrigerated sample into a membrane filtration cup; place the remaining 150 mL back in the 4°C refrigerator.
Label the filtration cup or the benchtop paper in front of it.
Verify seals on vacuum hoses and flask, then turn on the vacuum vent and the manifold valve for each sample.
Monitor flow until the sample is filtered (typically 30-45 minutes). The volume margin of error should be no more than 10% (15 mL).
Turn off the vacuum valve for the sample.
Using a 25 mL graduated pipette and automatic repeater pipette, recover any remaining sample from the cup back into the beaker and measure the volume removed.
Remove the top half of the filtration cup.
Using sterilized forceps, roll the membrane filter (sample-side facing outwards) and place it into a labeled DNA LoBind tube.

steps.title: Secondary Membrane Filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the remaining sample volume and combine filters.

substeps.instruction: Place the DNA LoBind tube in a 4°C refrigerator.
Aseptically place a new 0.45 µM membrane filter paper onto the cup and reseal.
Using the 25 mL graduated pipette, replace the previously measured recovered sample volume into the cup and open the vacuum valve.
Once filtered, remove the top cup, roll the second membrane (sample-side outwards), and place it into the same DNA LoBind tube.
Add the remaining 400 µL of Buffer RLT (Qiagen #79216) to the tube to reach a total volume of 800 µL.
Store the DNA LoBind tubes in a 4°C refrigerator.

steps.title: Viral Particle Release and RNA Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract RNA from the captured viral particles on the filters.

substeps.instruction: Vortex the DNA LoBind tubes using a vortex adapter for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the tube for 3 minutes at maximal speed.
Pipette the available liquid into a new labeled tube, pushing the filter aside to collect approximately 700 µL of sample liquid.
Add an equal volume of 70% molecular ethanol (e.g., 700 µL) to the sample and mix by pipetting up and down; do not vortex.
Transfer 700 µL of the mixture into a labeled RNeasy spin column and centrifuge for 30 seconds at full speed; discard filtrate. Repeat until all sample is filtered.
Transfer the spin column to a new 2 mL collection tube, centrifuge for 1 minute at full speed, and discard the tube and filtrate.
Place the spin column into a labeled 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube and add 50 µL of RNA-free water to the center; incubate for 1 minute at room temperature.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at full speed.
Add another 50 µL of RNA-free water to the center; incubate for 1 minute at room temperature.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at full speed to obtain a final volume of 100 µL of RNA.
Store the RNA at -20°C.

steps.title: Cleanup and Decontamination
steps.instruction: Clean all equipment and the biological hood according to safety protocols.

substeps.instruction: Dispose of biohazard bags in the correct floor trash can.
Wash all contaminated glassware, centrifuge bottles, and filtration cups with concentrated bleach to remove solids, then wash with lab-grade soap and hot water before placing on a drying rack.
Autoclave materials according to lab procedures.
Spray the biological hood and manifold with 10% bleach, wipe with paper towels, then repeat with 70% ethanol.
Turn off hood vents and lights.
Dispose of liquid from the vacuum flask and hoses into a biological hazard container.
Wash vacuum hoses with a 2:1 mixture of hot water and concentrated bleach; pour concentrated bleach into the vacuum flask to cover the bottom.
Perform a final spray of the hood with 10% bleach followed by 70% ethanol and wipe clean.
Reattach the vacuum flask and hoses to the vent.
Place two pieces of benchtop paper under the vacuum apparatus.

steps.title: Forceps Sterilization
steps.instruction: Maintain aseptic conditions for forceps throughout the process.

substeps.instruction: Pour 100% ethanol into a small autoclaved beaker.
Submerge the forceps in 100% ethanol, remove, and burn off the ethanol with a flame.
Place sterilized forceps in the hood without touching any physical surface.
Re-sterilize forceps using this method whenever they contact a contaminated surface or filter paper.
